description: methodology 1.5 — regularization: weight decay measured as a substitute for dropout and rejected, and the super-additivity of the two places dropout sits. The shipped fit carries dropout twice — COLUMN dropout over the wide feature region (activations and bot pass rates, every column dropped independently) and dropout between the trunk's hidden layers — and ships NO weight decay. Six configurations, twelve arms: the shipped fit; the feature-side dropout removed; the trunk's removed; BOTH removed; weight decay added with both dropouts intact; and weight decay with both dropouts off, which is the substitution the paragraph rejects. EVERY ARM HOLDS OUT WHOLE PROBLEMS (stop_unit=problem), and that is the crux of this panel rather than a detail of it: memorization means fitting problems the model has already seen at the expense of ones it has not, so a row-wise split — which leaves every problem partly trained — is the one split that cannot see it, and an arm that fingerprints its own training problems is REWARDED by it. The shipped row split is a convergence detector and is deliberately not used anywhere here. EVERY CONFIGURATION RUNS AT TWO SEEDS. The seed drives the held-out draw as well as the initialization, so within one seed every arm holds aside the same problems and a cross-arm delta is paired, while no cross-seed delta is quotable — a difference between two seeds is a difference between two holdout draws. What the second seed buys is a second independent estimate of the same paired delta, and agreement in SIGN between the two is what a contrast is quoted on. That matters more here than in most panels: the shipped configuration's own held-out score wanders across the last third of its budget by more than some of the contrasts this panel is asked about, so a single arm per configuration would resolve them only by accident. ONE DECAY VALUE, NOT A SWEEP: both decay arms run Adam weight decay at 0.0001, the conventional value for a network of this size, fixed before the panel ran rather than picked from its outcome. It is a single point on purpose — the paragraph's claim is about KIND, that a norm penalty does not do what dropout does because a low-norm readout of a near-unique high-dimensional code still fingerprints, and not about amount — and a sweep would multiply the panel's cost while still being unable to prove that no value works. What a single point cannot do is rule out some other decay value behaving differently, and nothing read off this panel may be stated as though it had. The knob is torch.optim.Adam's own weight_decay, which reaches EVERY parameter group, the network and the free per-user fields alike, so the decay arms carry an L2 on ability and on the axis positions as well, where the shipped design leaves ability unpenalized by construction. That is what the substitution on offer actually is; a decay confined to the trunk would be a different experiment and this panel does not run it.
